note: File: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl (in git; read from the worktree, copied out of git HEAD into runs/theory-tests/ if missing). Every row has attempt, cap_hit (boolean), finish_reason, score_v3 and n_new, so the finish_reason fallback is never used. Implemented as written: Mantel-Haenszel weights ME_p/M_p and ML_p/M_p, problems with M_p == 0 skipped, a zero denominator gives refuted_without_number. The recipe is unambiguous, so alt_measured is the crude pooled (unstratified) late/early rate ratio over the same rows. It is a comparison number, not another reading: the rival puts the stratified MH ratio near the crude ratio. n = problems with M_p > 0. Bootstrap resamples per-problem (E, ME, L, ML) tuples; a resample with a zero denominator scores inf. Caution: problems with no right finish in either window add nothing to the statistic, so the ratio depends on the few problems that have early or late events, and the interval may be wide.

Same base cue file. Long problems = at least one kept attempt-0 cap hit; of those, keep problems with >= 2 right finishes. d = |ln(max(n_i,1)/max(n_j,1))| over all unordered pairs within a problem, pooled; median takes the mean of the two middle values when the count is even. Fewer than 5 pairs gives refuted_without_number. Ambiguity: pooling pairs gives a problem with 3 rights 3 pairs and one with 2 rights 1 pair. Other reading (alt_measured): count each problem once, as the median over problems of each problem's median d. n = number of problems kept. Bootstrap resamples problems (each entry holds its tuple of right-finish lengths). Caution: a problem has at most 4 samples and needs a cap hit, so at most 3 rights and 3 pairs. The pooled set may be small, which makes the median coarse.

A = studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01/rows.jsonl, B = the base cue day1_3 file (both in git). attempt == 0 (a missing attempt counts as 0; every row has one), first row per (problem_index, sample). R counts right finishes with 12000 <= n_new < 16384. M sums max(0, min(n_new,16384)-12000)/1000 over all kept rows, cap hits included. M or R of B equal to 0 gives refuted_without_number. alt_measured is None: I found no real second reading (a cap hit's n_new is at least the cap, so counting cap-hit score_v3 == 1 rows would add no events inside the window). groups line: problems per file. n = min of the two. Bootstrap resamples problem_index with the A and B rows of a problem kept together, and recomputes both pooled rates. Caution: the base's late right count is probably small, around a dozen, so the ratio and its interval are sensitive to a few events.

Base cue day1_3 file. Z = problems whose kept attempt-0 rows (first per (problem_index, sample)) include at least one cap hit and no right finish. Restart rows = every row with attempt >= 1 in Z. Right = score_v3 == 1 and not a cap hit, applied to restart rows as well. No restart rows gives refuted_without_number. Ambiguity: the recipe defines Right next to the attempt-0 set, so it is unclear whether a restart row that hit the cap but has score_v3 == 1 counts. Other reading (alt_measured): count score_v3 == 1 alone. n = problems in Z with at least one restart row (the bootstrap unit). The rows number more. Caution: restarts happen only after a cap hit, so problems with more cap hits contribute more restart rows and pooling weights them more heavily.
